This Christmas, I was gifted a PS4 and AC: Unity. I know the game was panned at launch for running horribly, but is it worth playing nowadays? I liked Brotherhood and Shadow of Mordor, but the other AC games never really got me. Is the game worth it and how does it stack up to Syndicate?

EDIT: This seems to have been getting confused, so I'll just set the record straight. I own an unopened copy of Unity with a gift receipt. My question is not whether I should buy Unity, but whether I should keep it or return it and buy Syndicate instead.

I recently played it on my friend's PS4. He already downloaded the patch that fixes the glitches. So I didn't see anything wrong with it at least from glitches or bad textures. Umm, well, the story is forgetable really, although it's passable. The real life events are almost non existent, instead you're contacted by hackers and sometimes you are pulled into different time era's due to problems in the animus or something like that. Anyways, that's the story in a jiffy, there's so much more though.

If you are playing offline, and don't have online access play, well then you're missing around 50% of the game. There's a lot of missions that are online which isn't all that bad except you absolutely need it for 100% completion. Which sucks ass if you don't have access to good internet.

The game, is Beautiful. I cannot describe how it looks. It's just so sharp and well done. You'll have fun exploring the different areas, and being mesmerized by just how pretty everything is. Even if it's people rioting and protesting throughout most of the map. It's just so damm beautiful. Combat is like any other AC game, there's not much going on there. The game put a lot of effort and most of its time into missions and upgrades, clothing options and customization. Which is always good of course but the story suffered a lot. Although there's parts that are very memorable, like climbing the Eiffel Tower (Time Era Skip). But if there's one thing you'll love about this game, once you patch up, which is around 6 gbs.... The Enviroment. It's BEAUTIFUL.

If you can find this game cheap around 20 or so, it's a great investment. If not, wait a bit. I'm a big time fan of AC games, but don't own a PS4, so my friend let me borrow his to play Unity, and it was very much appreciated. Worth a playthrough for sure.

I would say the combat system has improved slightly as it's not really counter-instantkill anymore; they have health bars now. Since takes a while to bring down people, the game makes you resort to silent assassinations more often.

Agree with you on the other points though.

Ah yes, the combat system was slightly harder. I'm surprised I didn't remember much about it. I guess to me it was forgettable. Nope, all I remember from the fights was a lot of stealth and the last mission. If you're going for 100% synch you're going to be frustrated.

The Skill level up system was okay, but again without online access you didn't have enough points for all the skills on the list so I passed it without most of those.

That's good to know, I found the combat system incredibly dull after being reused with only slight changes, since AC II. The detailed historical settings were the only thing that really interested me in the series, but other improvements or gameplay changes are good for keeping the game fresh. I might consider getting Unity, when it's really cheap.

The game isn't that bad really. If you ignore the glitches, most of which are fixed by now, it's a pretty good game.

Bad things: I consider the story to be subpar, although it has been since ACIII, because it seems a bit too cliche. They focus way too much on Arno/Elise love story which leaves me wanting to hear more about the French Revolution/Assassin-Templar feud.

Another thing that the game is rather lacking are weapon choices. Yes, there are multiple types of weapons to choose from. But, after progressing through their level system, they all have an endgame that is far more powerful than its predecessors. For example, when you get the Sword of Eden, you can just go rampaging around with the same sword throughout the entire game. I would say that it would have been nice to have more weapons variety with unique strengths and weaknesses.

Good things: The game really shines in making an amazing world; it really makes you feel like you're in Paris with the level of detail they put into it. My favorite thing to do in the game is to run around the entire city to explore it.

They also improved the combat system. No longer is it a counter-kill shitfest from ACIII and ACIV. They made combat more difficult which also helps incentivizes you to avoid attacking large groups head on. It's not Dishonored level of difficulty as you can still easily kill people with the endgame weapons, but it's better than before.

Another thing they helped improve in the game was adding little Assassin events that aided you in taking out your target. It's generally a pretty simple side quest, but it is nice to see some variety in the actual assassinations.

Generally, AC: Unity is a decently good game. I hope you have fun with it.

I didn't play Unity until after patch 5 fixed the performance issues and got rid of the companion app BS, so I never experienced the worst of it. And I have to say, I really enjoyed it. The story is kind of lame and inconsequential, but the game is absolutely gorgeous, the parkour is fluid, the co-op is fun, and it's a ton of fun just exploring Paris. I got it on PC for about $25, which felt like a reasonable value.

I will say that Syndicate is measurably better in pretty much every way, though, save for its nonexistent multiplayer. That's a blast to play, and the Jack the Ripper DLC is pretty great as well. If you only have the funds for one, definitely go for Syndicate. But Unity is well worth a play now that it's no longer a disaster.
